runs.name: NRG Energy, Inc.; NYSE NRG, Delaware, 10-K filer; competitive power generation and retail electricity and gas in Texas and the U.S. Northeast; Direct Energy (2021), Vivint Smart Home (2023), LS Power plants (2026)
runs.box: TOO HARD (NATURE) AT Q2; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: The v5 re-run order at the operator's word ("Yes start with those"), interactive dispatch under the canonical brief, five analysts in parallel (NRG, OGE, PAM, PCG, PNW), lock held by the main session; the brief's one departure is the repository path after the move of 2026-10-25. Price **$92.31** (2026-10-23, aggregator, flagged) x **210,210,483 shares** (one class, 10-Q cover `0001013871-26-000020`) = cap **$19,405M**; sovereign **5.33%** (Treasury 30-year, 2026-10-23). Q1 IN, narrowly, by parts: Texas decides at 73% of five-year operating profit, a readable spread between retail price and supply cost; read as a whole after the LS Power purchase (plant $3.6B to $14.1B) it would close TOO HARD at Q1, and the file says so. Q2 TOO HARD (NATURE): the filer lists price first among why households choose a supplier; its Texas fleet is not low-cost (heat rate 11,087, 45% coal) and supplies about a third of Texas sales; Texas home customers 3,024k (2021) to 2,860k (2025) while Vistra's grew; no filing discloses churn, cost to serve or a price premium; storms (Uri $1,069M gross, $689M repaid by a state securitization), ERCOT rules that change every session and legislative limits on retail choice are forecasts no insider writes down. Not OUT: returns on tangible assets about 8% over the decade beat the integrated rivals. Competitors (pre-tax operating income on tangible assets, whole span): NRG 8.1%, VST 4.2%, CEG 3.5%, TLN 1.4% (from a sub-agent's EDGAR reading, not re-verified by the analyst). COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash before interest, taxed at 25%, $1,229M a year after all spending, $1,423M maintenance only (2021 to 2025), plus about $792M for the LS Power plants on their one audited year; two confessed CONVENTIONs raise it (the $3.3B of Direct Energy hedge receipts booked as financing added back, $729M without; the tax shelter valued apart at $1.66B); range **$80.80 to $92.62 a share all-equity (central)**, the price at the top; fair price **-$4.62 all-equity**, $62.79 equity-only beside; no case earns the floor (5.1% to 5.3%). Facts after the stop: equity negative in 2018, run down by buybacks, rebuilt by $3.7B of stock issued for LS Power; goodwill and intangibles $1.2B to $11.0B; debt $5.9B to $23.3B; interest cover 0.7 times in 2023; 2025 and 2026 buybacks at $130 to $164, above the computed range; Vivint paid $224M on a verdict including $140M of punitive damages and operates under an FTC settlement. Dispatcher's check: check_framework PASS; pathspec commits, own paths only; 38 ids and 15 fragments clean (the analyst's check). Contamination declared: commit subjects, `.gitignore` text, daily file names; none opened. Position note filled at the fold: not held. No alert (closed before Q7).
runs.narr: TOO HARD (NATURE) at Q2: a Texas power retailer selling a commodity on price, without a low-cost fleet, losing home customers while its rival gains them, exposed to storms and to rules rewritten each legislative session. Computation only: range $80.80 to $92.62 all-equity vs $92.31, fair -$4.62. Bought back stock at $130 to $164 before the price fell to $92, then issued $3.7B of stock for LS Power.
